quiz.question_id: Mengapa `sync.WaitGroup` lebih baik daripada `time.Sleep` untuk menunggu goroutine?
quiz.question_en: Why is `sync.WaitGroup` better than `time.Sleep` for waiting on goroutines?
options_id: Karena `WaitGroup` selalu membuat goroutine parallel
Karena `WaitGroup` menghapus kebutuhan akan channel
Karena `WaitGroup` deterministik dan menunggu penyelesaian kerja yang nyata
Karena `time.Sleep` tidak bisa dipakai di Go
options_en: Because `WaitGroup` always makes goroutines parallel
Because `WaitGroup` removes the need for channels
Because `WaitGroup` is deterministic and waits for real work completion
Because `time.Sleep` cannot be used in Go

quiz.question_id: Urutan mana yang benar saat meluncurkan worker dengan `WaitGroup`?
quiz.question_en: Which order is correct when launching a worker with a `WaitGroup`?
options_id: `go worker(...); wg.Add(1)`
`wg.Add(1); go worker(...)`
`wg.Wait(); go worker(...)`
`go wg.Add(1); worker(...)`
options_en: `go worker(...); wg.Add(1)`
`wg.Add(1); go worker(...)`
`wg.Wait(); go worker(...)`
`go wg.Add(1); worker(...)`

options_id: Saat counter `WaitGroup` mencapai 0
Saat goroutine pertama selesai
Saat semua channel ditutup
Segera setelah `Add(1)` dipanggil
options_en: When the `WaitGroup` counter reaches 0
When the first goroutine finishes
When all channels are closed
Immediately after `Add(1)` is called

quiz.question_id: Mengapa `defer wg.Done()` biasanya diletakkan di awal worker?
quiz.question_en: Why is `defer wg.Done()` typically placed at the start of a worker?
options_id: Agar `Done` dipanggil sebelum kerja dimulai
Agar `WaitGroup` bisa di-copy dengan aman
Agar worker tidak perlu menerima parameter lain
Agar counter tetap dikurangi meski terjadi return awal atau panic
options_en: So `Done` is called before the work starts
So the `WaitGroup` can be copied safely
So the worker does not need any other parameters
So the counter is still decremented even if there is an early return or panic

quiz.question_id: Apa risiko memanggil `wg.Add(1)` di dalam goroutine yang baru dibuat?
quiz.question_en: What is the risk of calling `wg.Add(1)` inside the newly launched goroutine?
options_id: `WaitGroup` otomatis menjadi negatif
`wg.Wait()` bisa melihat counter masih nol dan selesai terlalu cepat sebelum `Add` terjadi
Goroutine tidak akan pernah mulai
`Done()` otomatis menjadi no-op
options_en: The `WaitGroup` automatically becomes negative
`wg.Wait()` may still see the counter as zero and return too early before `Add` happens
The goroutine will never start
`Done()` automatically becomes a no-op

quiz.question_id: Mengapa parameter worker bertipe `*sync.WaitGroup` dan bukan `sync.WaitGroup`?
quiz.question_en: Why is the worker parameter type `*sync.WaitGroup` instead of `sync.WaitGroup`?
options_id: Agar semua goroutine berbagi counter yang sama, bukan salinan
Agar method `Done()` bisa dipanggil tanpa `defer`
Agar worker otomatis menjadi OS thread
Agar `Wait()` tidak pernah memblokir
options_en: So all goroutines share the same counter instead of copies
So the `Done()` method can be called without `defer`
So the worker automatically becomes an OS thread
So `Wait()` never blocks

quiz.question_id: Pada contoh fan-out, mengapa ada goroutine terpisah yang menjalankan `wg.Wait()` lalu `close(results)`?
quiz.question_en: In the fan-out example, why is there a separate goroutine that runs `wg.Wait()` and then `close(results)`?
options_id: Untuk mengurutkan hasil berdasarkan item asal
Untuk menambah kapasitas channel `results` saat runtime
Agar loop `range results` tahu kapan semua pengiriman selesai dan bisa berhenti
Agar setiap worker menutup channelnya sendiri
options_en: To sort results by the original item
To increase the `results` channel capacity at runtime
So the `range results` loop knows when all sends are finished and can stop
So each worker closes its own channel

quiz.question_id: Apa yang mungkin terjadi jika `results` tidak pernah ditutup pada contoh fan-out?
quiz.question_en: What may happen if `results` is never closed in the fan-out example?
options_id: `range` akan otomatis berhenti saat buffer kosong
Receiver yang melakukan `range` bisa menunggu selamanya setelah semua nilai habis
Semua hasil akan hilang sebelum dicetak
`WaitGroup` akan panic saat `Wait()` dipanggil
options_en: The `range` will automatically stop when the buffer is empty
The receiver ranging over the channel may wait forever after all values are consumed
All results will be lost before they are printed
The `WaitGroup` will panic when `Wait()` is called

quiz.question_id: Istilah fan-out pada lesson berarti apa?
quiz.question_en: What does the term fan-out mean in the lesson?
options_id: Menggabungkan banyak channel menjadi satu
Membuat satu goroutine membaca semua file
Memindahkan pekerjaan dari goroutine ke OS thread
Membagi satu kumpulan pekerjaan ke banyak goroutine
options_en: Combining many channels into one
Making one goroutine read all files
Moving work from a goroutine to an OS thread
Distributing one set of work across many goroutines

quiz.question_id: Mengapa `results := make(chan int, len(items))` cocok pada contoh fan-out?
quiz.question_en: Why is `results := make(chan int, len(items))` a good fit in the fan-out example?
options_id: Karena channel harus selalu buffered untuk dipakai dengan `WaitGroup`
Karena `len(items)` mengubah channel menjadi send-only
Karena setiap worker bisa mengirim satu hasil tanpa menunggu receive langsung dari collector
Karena `close(results)` hanya bekerja pada channel penuh
options_en: Because a channel must always be buffered when used with a `WaitGroup`
Because `len(items)` makes the channel send-only
Because each worker can send one result without waiting for an immediate receive from the collector
Because `close(results)` only works on full channels
